I like to cruise /v/all, however it will get filled with what I consider chaff, stuff I'd rather not have clogging my view.

To that end, I'd like to be able to filter out content that is undesirable to me. I'd like the filters to be easily shareable by giving out a link or something similar.

For transparency sake, every subverse, user, title keyword, and message keyword should be shown in some sort of sortable statistics page. This way you could see that the /v/KiltedKenIsGreat subverse is the most popularly hidden subverse, or that /user/KiltedKen has been filtered-out by 421 other users.

Moderators would see everything in the subverses they moderate -- to ensure they can do their job.

I think this is beneficial to a site free of censorship, because while I support not censoring anyone in general, I don't necessarily want to read posts from particular subverses or users.
Feature that allows user to filter/hide/ignore content based on: subverse, other user, title keyword, message keyword - filters should be shareable
sharing filters - no way. ignore a sub feature? yes.
I'm extra curious why you'd not share your filters with friends.

On reddit one of the first subs I filtered was the rage comics sub. I haven't found a need for a filter yet but I know it's inevitable and would love the option to filter or hide links that I have no interest in.
I think this is a pretty good idea actually. It's not really censorship because the post is still on the website for everyone. Unless of course the user filtered it out, but that is his choice.

What if users were able to set up censoring for themselves by themselves depending on what they actually wanted to see. Voat's ability to block subverses is a really great idea, but what if it extended to include the ability to block posts with certain keywords, for example, racial slurs, This way the white supremacists and SJW hunters can circlejerk all day long, and everybody else can filter them out. Obviously it isn't a perfect solution, but at least it's some sort of method of cutting down on the amount of low quality posts we'd have to sift through. Even better if you can share your filtering rules with others.
